text:
marta: quick sync — we need an interface for the obs-catalog so runtime can publish lightweight envelopes and analytics can do late enrichment without pulling cost attribution apart. thinking: minimal envelope + stable billing_keys. thoughts?

sam: +1. main tradeoff: include billing_keys in envelope vs do lookup in ingest. if we put keys in envelope we preserve accuracy but increase payload and coupling.

tyler: lookup has failure modes (late joins). For cost accuracy we need deterministic propagation at edge when available. maybe envelope should carry optional billing_key and a provenance header.

leah: can we keep billing keys optional but also carry a fingerprint for late resolution? e.g. `cost_fingerprint` so later joiners can at least approximate.

devin: quick sketch of proto: 
```
ObsEnvelope {
  trace_id: string
  timestamp: int64
  payload: bytes
  billing_keys?: { tenant_id?: string, cost_key?: string }
  cost_fingerprint?: string
  provenance: string   // edge | runtime | enrich
}
```

marta: yeah that matches. question: how to handle sampled traces? if sampled out at edge we can't attach billing_keys. fallback: store a minimal sample header that includes billing_keys hashed with salt? privacy concerns.

sam: hashed keys -> good for privacy, but then analytics needs salt to decode. better: have two fields: `billing_keys_plain` (only when allowed) and `billing_keys_hash` which is always set. policy enforcement required.

ingest-bot: deploy finished for obs-schema-microchange (build #522) :white_check_mark:

leah: operational concern: cardinality explosion if we carry many tenant attributes. suggest limit to `tenant_id` + `cost_key` + `tier`. others are tags resolved in enrichment step.

tyler: agree. Also add TTL on enrich joins to handle late-arriving keys — prevents unbounded backfill.

marta: next steps: 1) agree on minimal envelope proto 2) add policy for plain vs hashed keys 3) implement ingest enrichment adapter that consumes `cost_fingerprint` and tries resolution. I'll draft RFC. @sam can you add a few example failure modes?

sam: will do. adding a short list in RFC: late-enrich misses, hashed-salt mismatch, sampling gaps, multi-tenant aggregation mismatches. Also include perf numbers for extra ~24 bytes per envelope (measured on a small trace simulator).

devin: I'll prototype the adapter and a sim for sampling scenarios.

marta: thanks — meeting to finalize RFC on Thursday 11am. :calendar:
